notes: Google documents Gemini Robotics ER 2 Streaming Preview as the low-latency robotics endpoint for real-time bidirectional interaction through the Live API.
The model accepts text, image, video, and audio input and returns text output.
Google declares a 131,072-token input limit and a 65,536-token output limit.
The dedicated streaming endpoint uses a stateful WebSocket connection integrated with the Live API.
Function calling, Live API, search grounding, and thinking are supported.
Caching, code execution, computer use, file search, Google Maps grounding, image generation, structured outputs, URL context, and Batch API are explicitly unsupported.
Audio generation, Flex inference, and Priority inference are explicitly unsupported.
Google's robotics streaming guide states that only blocking function calls are supported for robotics Live API tool execution.
Parallel function calling and MCP support are not declared in the checked model documentation and remain unknown.
